title: The e-CALLISTO FITS Downloader
html:
The e-CALLISTO FITS Downloader

The e-CALLISTO FITS Downloader retrieves FITS files directly from the e-CALLISTO data archive. Open it with the Download toolbar tool, Download > Launch FITS Downloader, or Solar Events > Radio Bursts > e-CALLISTO.

The window has four tabs — Single Station, Multi-Station Event, Spectral Overview and Burst List — described in the sections below. Station lists are read from the archive whenever a date changes, so they offer only the stations that have data on the chosen UTC days; a line under the date reports how many, for example 42 stations have data on 2026-10-04 (UTC).

Common features

The download cache

Previewed and downloaded files are kept in a persistent cache on disk, so re-previewing, importing or extending a dataset never fetches the same file twice. The size of the cache is shown at the bottom left of the window (Cache: …). Open Cache Folder opens the cache in the file manager and Clear Cache empties it.

Preview, download, import and compare

The tabs share four actions on the files you have ticked:

Preview

opens the FITS Preview window with a background-subtracted spectrogram of the selection. A selection that can be combined in time, in frequency or in both is previewed as it would be imported; otherwise each file appears in its own tab.

Download

asks for a folder (Select Download Folder) and saves the files there.

Import

loads the selection into the main window, combining it automatically when possible (Section 5.3). Gap and overlap options are requested when needed.

Compare

opens the Multi-Station Comparison with the selection (Chapter 12).

During downloads a progress panel shows the overall progress, transfer statistics and an estimated time remaining; Show file details expands a table with the progress, speed and status of every file.

Single Station

The Single Station tab (Figure 11.1) lists all files of one station for a complete UTC day.

  1. In Observation Parameters, choose the Date and then the Station.

  2. Click Show Available FITS.

  3. In Available FITS Files (Whole Day, grouped by focus code), expand a focus code and tick files, or tick a whole focus-code group. Each group heading shows the number of files and the time span covered, for example Focus 63 — 34 files (00:00–08:14), so the receivers that covered an event are visible at a glance.

  4. Use the buttons in Actions: Select All, Deselect All, Download Selected, Preview Selected, Compare or Import.

When several files are ticked, the downloader determines whether they can be combined in time, in frequency or in both, using the rules of Section 5.3. Files that cannot be combined are reported with an explanation (Figure 5.1).

Multi-Station Event

The Multi-Station Event tab (Figure 11.2) finds the files recorded by several stations during the same event in a single search.

  1. In Event Window, set Start (UTC) and Stop (UTC). The station list is updated to the stations with data in that window (windows of up to seven days).

  2. In Stations, tick the stations to search. Filter stations narrows the list by name; Select All and Clear tick or untick all stations.

  3. Click Search Matching FITS. The Matching FITS Files table lists the station, UTC time, file name and receiver (focus code) of every file overlapping the window.

  4. Use Select All, Clear Selection, Download Selected, Import or Compare.

A compatible selection is imported directly into the main window, combined in time, in frequency or in both. Files from several stations cannot be combined into one spectrum; use Compare to view them side by side. The comparison workspace opens only when Compare is clicked.

Spectral Overview

The Spectral Overview tab (Figure 11.3) assembles a station’s observations for a complete UTC day into one overview figure.

Date (UTC), Station

the day and station to summarize.

Focus code

All available focus codes, or a single focus code to generate or regenerate on its own.

Generate Overview

downloads (or reuses from the cache) every file of the day and builds the overview. The status line reports the focus codes generated and the number of files loaded. Cancel stops a running generation.

one tab per focus code. Each overview shows the day as six four-hour panels (00–04 UT to 20–24 UT), background-subtracted with a day-wide median (dB) baseline and a common color scale; intervals without data are marked No data.

The Burst List tab (Figure 11.4) gives access to the e-CALLISTO solar radio burst catalog compiled by C. Monstein (Monstein, n.d.), so that the FITS files for a listed burst can be found together with its type and reporting stations. The Monstein source catalog link opens the original lists in a web browser.

Catalog filters
From (UTC), Through (UTC)

the date range to load; click Load Events.

Burst type

All types or one of the burst types found in the loaded catalog (for example II or III).

Reporting station

events reported by a given station.

Min. stations

events reported by at least this many stations (Any for no limit).

Search

free-text search in the type, stations or remarks.

Reset Filters

clears the filters while keeping the selected dates.

A progress bar with a Cancel button reports catalog loading, FITS searches, preview preparation and downloads. The final state remains visible after completion.

1. Choose a burst

The event table lists the start and end time (UTC), type, number of stations, and the observatories and remarks of each matching event, with a count such as 1 of 2 events match the filters. Station

All reported stations, one of them, or the name of any archive station typed in the box.

padding added on both sides of the burst (0–120 min, default 2 min).

searches the archive. Overlapping 15-minute files and events that cross UTC midnight are included. The table lists the station, start time, focus code and file name of each file found.

act on the ticked files as described above; the number of selected files is shown.

title: Multi-Station Comparison
html:
Multi-Station Comparison

The Multi-Station Comparison workspace displays dynamic spectra from several stations in vertically stacked panels with a shared time axis, so that the same event can be compared across stations, receivers and frequency ranges (Figure 12.1). It is opened from View > Multi-Station Comparison... or with the Compare button of the downloader (Chapter 11).

The workspace follows the rendering mode of the application: in Modern mode the panels are hardware-accelerated when available, and in Classic mode they are drawn with Matplotlib.

Stations and files

The Stations / Files group lists the loaded files as station – date – file name. Add Files... adds FITS files from disk, Remove removes the selected entry and Clear removes all entries. Files that can be combined are merged automatically before display: each station’s files are combined in time, in frequency, or as a complete time ×\times focus-code grid (Section 5.3), so a mixed-station selection yields one panel per station. Hovering over an entry shows any warning raised while reading it.

Display controls

Display controls of the Multi-Station Comparison.
Group Control Function
View Time alignment UT clock aligns the panels on Universal Time; Seconds from file start aligns each panel on its own start. UT alignment requires TIME-OBS in every file; otherwise the workspace switches to seconds and says so.
Appearance Units Digits or dB.
Colormap Color map of all panels.
Color scale Shared scale (one scale for all panels), Per-station auto scale, or Manual scale with Low and High limits.
Noise Reduction Target All panels or one panel.
Method None, Mean background, Median background, Robust background or Noise clipping.
Colormap Color map of the noise-reduced panels.
Thresholds With Noise clipping, Lower threshold and Upper threshold sliders and a Logarithmic Threshold Scale option, as in the main window.

Display range and view configurations

The Actions group contains:

Set Range...

enter a shared time and frequency range for all panels.

Reset Range

return to the full range of the data.

Load View Config...

apply a .efaview.json view configuration (Section 7.2.2). The visual settings are applied; when the files differ in date, set UT bounds with Set Range....

Export...

export the comparison (Section 12.5).

Ruler measurement

In the Measurement group, Start Ruler activates a ruler: click two points in one panel to measure the duration, frequency drift and slope, shown under Readout. Clear removes the measurement.

Exporting a comparison

Export... opens the Export Comparison dialog (Figure 12.2):

Visible View

exports the comparison exactly as it appears in the window.

Grid / Table Layout

exports a compact publication-style matrix of all panels, with a shared time axis, each station’s native frequency range and a white background. Its options are the number of Columns (Auto or a fixed number), an Overall title, and the Raster resolution (DPI) for bitmap formats.

The figure can be saved as PNG, PDF, EPS, SVG or TIFF.

title: Learmonth and STEREO/SWAVES Data
html:
Learmonth and STEREO/SWAVES Data

Besides the e-CALLISTO archive, the application reads data from two further radio instruments: the ground-based Learmonth Solar Radio Spectrograph in Western Australia, and the space-based STEREO/WAVES (SWAVES) radio receivers. Both are opened from Solar Events > Radio Bursts.

Learmonth Solar Radio Spectrograph

The Learmonth Solar Radio Spectrograph, operated by the Australian Bureau of Meteorology, records daily archive files (.srs) in two receiver bands. Solar Events > Radio Bursts > Learmonth opens the Learmonth Solar Radio Browser (Figure 13.1), which converts selected parts of a daily file into FIT files for the main window.

Observation Parameters

choose the Date and a Time, then click Show Available Data. The daily file is read from the local cache when available and downloaded otherwise. The chunk containing the chosen time is highlighted.

Daily Raw File

information about the daily archive file. Download saves the raw .srs file to a folder you choose.

Available 15-Minute Chunks

the time ranges into which the day is divided. Select All and Deselect All change the selection.

Convert to FIT

converts the selected chunks to CALLISTO-style FIT files in a folder you choose.

Convert and Import

converts the selected chunks and imports them into the main window, combined in time when consecutive.

Converted files carry a standard FITS header with the frequency and time axes and the observatory position, so they can be processed and analyzed exactly like e-CALLISTO data.

STEREO/SWAVES

SWAVES on the twin STEREO spacecraft (Bougeret et al. 2008) records radio spectra from 2.6 kHz to 16 MHz, directly below the CALLISTO band. A burst that drifts out of the ground-based range can therefore be followed into the interplanetary medium on the same figure. Solar Events > Radio Bursts > SWAVES opens the STEREO/SWAVES Radio Spectrograph dialog (Figure 13.2).

Start date, Start time, Duration

the UTC window to load (0.1–24 h; default 4 h). The data are NASA/SPDF level-2 one-minute averages served as one file per UTC day; a window that crosses midnight fetches and joins both days. The archive starts on 27 October 2006, and downloaded day files are cached and reused.

Spacecraft

STEREO-A (Ahead) or STEREO-B (Behind). STEREO-B is unavailable for dates after 1 October 2014, when contact with the spacecraft was lost.

Sync padding

extra time added on each side when the window is taken from the CALLISTO spectrum (0–720 min; default 30 min). A Type II or Type III burst takes tens of minutes to hours to drift from the corona into the SWAVES band, so an exact match would cut off the part you want to see.

Use CALLISTO Window

copies the time range of the loaded CALLISTO spectrum, widened by the sync padding. Solar Events > Sync Current Time Window updates an open SWAVES dialog in the same way.

Download and Plot

loads the data; Cancel stops a running load.

The split view

Once SWAVES data are loaded, the plotting area of the main window splits into two panels: CALLISTO above and SWAVES below, on a shared time axis, so that panning or zooming either panel moves both (Figure 13.3). The CALLISTO interval is outlined on the SWAVES panel. The SWAVES frequency axis is always logarithmic and its intensity is in decibels above the instrument background, so the panel keeps its own color bar and color scaling while following the color map chosen in the sidebar. Loading SWAVES with no CALLISTO file open plots it across the whole area; it moves into the split view as soon as a FITS file is loaded.

Solar Events > SWAVES Panel hides and restores the panel without discarding the loaded data. The split view is included in exported figures, saved in and restored from projects without downloading the data again, and added to project reports.

Note

The drawing, lasso, drift and measurement tools act on the CALLISTO panel only, and the data-reduction controls of the sidebar do not apply to the SWAVES panel.

title: Solar-Event Viewers
html:
Solar-Event Viewers

The viewers in the Solar Events menu place a radio event in its wider context: the X-ray flare, energetic protons, the geomagnetic response and any associated coronal mass ejection. Each viewer is an independent window that fetches its data from the archive listed in Appendix C. The viewers can also be started from source as standalone programs (Section 2.5).

Common controls

The GOES and geomagnetic viewers share a common layout:

  • a time-range selector with Start and End rows (date, and hour, minute or three-hour slot) and, where applicable, the spacecraft;

  • a Preset list with Apply for common ranges;

  • a plot button that fetches and plots the data, with a progress indicator;

  • Save Plot (PNG) and Save Data (CSV);

  • a reset or clear button; and

  • an information panel summarizing the plotted data or a selected interval.

Synchronizing the time window

Solar Events > Sync Current Time Window sends the time range of the spectrum loaded in the main window to every open context window: the GOES X-ray and proton viewers, the Dst and Kp viewers and the STEREO/SWAVES dialog plot the new range; the SOHO/LASCO CME catalog searches the day of the middle of the range; and the SunPy Explorer takes the range as its query window. The status bar reports which windows were updated, or that none were open.

GOES X-ray flux

Solar Events > Flares > GOES X-Ray Flux opens the GOES XRS Plotter (Figure 14.1), which plots the soft X-ray flux measured by the GOES X-Ray Sensor in its short (XRS-A, 0.05–0.4 nm) and long (XRS-B, 0.1–0.8 nm) channels.

Start, End, Use

the UTC range and the spacecraft (GOES-8 to GOES-19; default GOES-16). Preset: Whole day (00:00–23:59) selects the whole of the start day.

Plot XRS Data

downloads the daily science files from NOAA and plots both channels on a logarithmic flux axis.

Selection

drag across the plot to select a flare interval. The Flare Information panel then shows the Selection window, the Peak X-ray Flux (W/m²) and Peak Time (UTC) of the long channel, the Rise Time (selection start to peak), the Decay Time (peak to selection end), the Flare Duration and the GOES Class derived from the peak flux.

Save Plot, Save Data, Reset

save the figure as PNG, save the fluxes as CSV, or clear the plot and selection.

GOES overlay on the spectrum

Solar Events > GOES Overlay > Short(XRS-A) and Long(XRS-B) draw the GOES X-ray curves directly on the dynamic spectrum in the main window (Figure 14.2), with a flare-class guide (A, B, C, M, X) on the right. The overlay does not modify the spectrum data. The application chooses a GOES satellite appropriate for the date automatically, falling back across legacy and modern satellites when a file is unavailable. The overlay is included in exported figures.

GOES proton flux

Solar Events > Energetic Particles > GOES SEP Proton Flux opens the GOES SEP Proton Flux Plotter (Figure 14.3), which plots proton fluxes from the GOES Solar and Galactic Proton Sensor (SGPS) archive at NOAA over multi-day UTC ranges.

Start, End, Use

the UTC range and the spacecraft: Auto (GOES-19 -> GOES-16) tries the newest spacecraft first, or a specific GOES satellite can be chosen.

Preset

Last 24 hours, Last 72 hours, Last 7 days or Current UTC day.

Plot SEP Proton Flux

fetches and stitches the daily files and plots the channels closest to about 10 MeV and 100 MeV, with hover readouts.

Selection

drag across the plot to measure an event.

SEP Analysis

the spacecraft, channels, number of samples and source files, the peaks of both channels in the plot, and for the selection its window, peak (low channel), peak time, rise time, decay time and duration.

Save Plot, Save Data, Clear Selection

save the figure as PNG, save the stitched flux table as CSV, or clear the selection.

Kyoto Dst index

Solar Events > Geomagnetic > Kyoto Dst Index opens the Dst Index viewer (Figure 14.4) for the hourly Dst index from the World Data Center for Geomagnetism, Kyoto (Nosé et al. 2015). Dst measures the strength of the ring current; large negative values indicate geomagnetic storms.

Start, End

date and hour. Preset: Last 24 hours, Last 7 days, Current month or Previous month.

Plot Dst Data

fetches and plots the index with storm-level guides at 0 (quiet), −50-50, −100-100 and −200-200 nT.

Dst Summary

the number of samples, the data sources (final, provisional or real-time), and the minimum, maximum (each with its time) and mean Dst.

Save Plot, Save Data, Reset

PNG figure, CSV table, or clear.

GFZ Kp index

Solar Events > Geomagnetic > GFZ Kp Index opens the Kp Index viewer (Figure 14.5) for the three-hourly planetary Kp index from GFZ Potsdam (Matzka et al. 2021).

Start, End

date and three-hour slot (3h Slot). Preset: Last 24 hours, Last 7 days, Current month or Previous month.

Plot Kp Data

plots the index as bars colored by activity (quiet below 5, storm from 5, severe from 7), with guide lines at Kp 5, 7 and 8.

Kp Summary

the number of intervals, the maximum, minimum and mean Kp, and the number of storm intervals (Kp≥5\mathrm{Kp}\geq5).

Save Plot, Save Data, Reset

PNG figure, CSV table, or clear.

SOHO/LASCO CME catalog

Solar Events > CMEs > SOHO/LASCO CME Catalog opens the SOHO/LASCO CME Catalog Tool (Figure 14.6), which reads the CDAW catalog of CMEs observed by SOHO/LASCO (Yashiro et al. 2004).

Year, Month, Day, Search

list the CMEs of the chosen day. A progress bar shows the retrieval.

CME table

one row per CME with the columns Date and Time, Central PA, Angular Width, Linear Speed, Accel, Mass, Kinetic Energy, MPA (measurement position angle) and Remarks. Clicking a row shows its details beside the table.

Play Movie

plays the LASCO movie associated with the selected CME (double-clicking a row does the same) in a viewer with Back, Forward, Reload, Open in Browser, Open Raw Movie and Copy URL.

Open in Browser, Copy URL

open the CDAW page of the selected CME, or copy its address.

GOES overlay on the spectrum Solar Events > GOES Overlay > Short(XRS-A) and Long(XRS-B) draw the GOES X-ray curves directly on the dynamic spectrum in the main window (Figure 14.2 ), with a flare-class guide (A, B, C, M, X) on the right. The overlay does not modify the spectrum data. The application chooses a GOES satellite appropriate for the date automatically, falling back across legacy and modern satellites when a file is unavailable. The overlay is included in exported figures. Figure 14.2. GOES X-ray curves overlaid on a dynamic spectrum. View illustration in the PDF edition. GOES proton flux Solar Events > Energetic Particles > GOES SEP Proton Flux opens the GOES SEP Proton Flux Plotter (Figure 14.3 ), which plots proton fluxes from the GOES Solar and Galactic Proton Sensor (SGPS) archive at NOAA over multi-day UTC ranges. Figure 14.3. The GOES SEP Proton Flux Plotter. View illustration in the PDF edition. Start, End, Use the UTC range and the spacecraft: Auto (GOES-19 -> GOES-16) tries the newest spacecraft first, or a specific GOES satellite can be chosen. Preset Last 24 hours , Last 72 hours , Last 7 days or Current UTC day . Plot SEP Proton Flux fetches and stitches the daily files and plots the channels closest to about 10 MeV and 100 MeV, with hover readouts. Selection drag across the plot to measure an event. SEP Analysis the spacecraft, channels, number of samples and source files, the peaks of both channels in the plot, and for the selection its window, peak (low channel), peak time, rise time, decay time and duration. Save Plot, Save Data, Clear Selection save the figure as PNG, save the stitched flux table as CSV, or clear the selection. Kyoto Dst index Solar Events > Geomagnetic > Kyoto Dst Index opens the Dst Index viewer (Figure 14.4 ) for the hourly Dst index from the World Data Center for Geomagnetism, Kyoto ( Nosé et al. 2015 ) . Dst measures the strength of the ring current; large negative values indicate geomagnetic storms. Figure 14.4. The Kyoto Dst Index viewer. View illustration in the PDF edition. Start, End date and hour. Preset : Last 24 hours , Last 7 days , Current month or Previous month . Plot Dst Data fetches and plots the index with storm-level guides at 0 (quiet), − 50 , − 100 and − 200 nT. Dst Summary the number of samples, the data sources (final, provisional or real-time), and the minimum, maximum (each with its time) and mean Dst. Save Plot, Save Data, Reset PNG figure, CSV table, or clear. GFZ Kp index Solar Events > Geomagnetic > GFZ Kp Index opens the Kp Index viewer (Figure 14.5 ) for the three-hourly planetary Kp index from GFZ Potsdam ( Matzka et al. 2021 ) . Figure 14.5. The GFZ Kp Index viewer. View illustration in the PDF edition. Start, End date and three-hour slot ( 3h Slot ). Preset : Last 24 hours , Last 7 days , Current month or Previous month . Plot Kp Data plots the index as bars colored by activity (quiet below 5, storm from 5, severe from 7), with guide lines at Kp 5, 7 and 8. Kp Summary the number of intervals, the maximum, minimum and mean Kp, and the number of storm intervals ( K p ≥ 5 ). Save Plot, Save Data, Reset PNG figure, CSV table, or clear. SOHO/LASCO CME catalog Solar Events > CMEs > SOHO/LASCO CME Catalog opens the SOHO/LASCO CME Catalog Tool (Figure 14.6 ), which reads the CDAW catalog of CMEs observed by SOHO/LASCO ( Yashiro et al. 2004 ) . Figure 14.6. The SOHO/LASCO CME Catalog Tool. View illustration in the PDF edition. Year, Month, Day, Search list the CMEs of the chosen day. A progress bar shows the retrieval. CME table one row per CME with the columns Date and Time , Central PA , Angular Width , Linear Speed , Accel , Mass , Kinetic Energy , MPA (measurement position angle) and Remarks . Clicking a row shows its details beside the table. Play Movie plays the LASCO movie associated with the selected CME (double-clicking a row does the same) in a viewer with Back , Forward , Reload , Open in Browser , Open Raw Movie and Copy URL . Open in Browser, Copy URL open the CDAW page of the selected CME, or copy its address.

title: SunPy Multi-Mission Explorer
html:
SunPy Multi-Mission Explorer

The SunPy Multi-Mission Explorer searches public solar archives through SunPy (The SunPy Community et al. 2020), downloads the selected records into an application-managed cache, and plots images and time series for quick inspection. Open it with Solar Events > Archives > SunPy Multi-Mission Explorer. For in-depth image analysis, use Solar Image Analysis (Part V).

Supported instruments

Table 15.1 lists the instruments that can be searched. Map (image) products are shown in the plot window as image sequences; GOES/XRS is a time series.

Instruments available in the SunPy Multi-Mission Explorer.
Instrument Type Selectable options
SDO/AIA Map Wavelength 94, 131, 171, 193, 211, 304, 335, 1600, 1700 Å
SDO/HMI Map Product: magnetogram, continuum, dopplergram
SOHO/EIT Map Wavelength 171, 195, 284, 304 Å
SOHO/LASCO C2, C3 Map Detector
STEREO-A/B SECCHI Map Detector EUVI (171, 195, 284, 304 Å), COR1, COR2, HI1, HI2
GOES/SUVI Map Wavelength 94, 131, 171, 195, 284, 304 Å; level 1b or 2
PROBA2/SWAP Map —
GOES/XRS Time series GOES satellite

STEREO-B entries return data only for 2007–2014, before contact with the spacecraft was lost.

Searching the archives

The Archive Query group contains:

Spacecraft, Instrument

the observatory and instrument. The Detector, Wavelength (A), GOES Satellite, product and Level fields appear when they apply to the selected instrument.

Sample (s)

the sampling cadence in seconds; 0 requests the full archive cadence, which is slower and returns more records.

Start (UTC), End (UTC), Max Records

the time range and the maximum number of records returned.

Search Archives

runs the query. Retry Last Query repeats it, for example after a network error.

Use Analyzer Time Window

sets the time range from the spectrum in the main window and searches.

Open Cache Folder, Clear Cache

manage the download cache; its size is shown.

The Search Results table lists, for each record, the start and end time, source, instrument, provider, file identifier and size. Tick the records to download with the Use column or Select All and Clear Selection, then click Download & Load Selected. Retry Failed downloads again only the rows that failed, and Stop cancels a running search or download. Cached files can be reopened without a network connection.

The plot window

Open Plot Window in the Analysis and Export group opens the SunPy Plot and Animation window with the loaded data (Figure 15.2).

In map mode the controls are:

Frame slider

steps through the sequence; the frame number is shown.

Run Diff

shows running differences between consecutive frames. Difference > Base Difference shows each frame minus the first.

AIA Limb (EUVI)

on STEREO/EUVI images, draws the solar limb as seen from Earth, showing which part of the disk is visible to SDO/AIA.

NRGF

applies the normalizing-radial-graded filter (Morgan et al. 2006) to coronagraph images (COR1, COR2, LASCO), flattening the radial fall-off of brightness to reveal faint CME fronts.

Play, Pause, Rewind, FPS

animate the sequence at 1–30 frames per second.

Select ROI, Reset ROI

draw a rectangular region of interest on the map, for which the minimum, maximum, mean, median, standard deviation and 95th and 99th percentiles are computed.

In time-series mode (GOES/XRS) the window plots the X-ray channels and derives basic flare summary metrics.

Exporting

The Analysis and Export group of the explorer provides Save Files As..., which copies the downloaded data files to a folder of your choice; Export Plot, which saves the current plot as PNG, PDF, SVG, TIFF or JPG; and Export Analysis CSV, which saves the ROI statistics or flare summary.

title: The Solar Image Analysis Window
html:
The Solar Image Analysis Window

Solar Image Analysis is a multi-mission imaging workspace for extreme-ultraviolet (EUV) disk images, magnetograms, coronagraph images and heliospheric images. It retrieves image sequences from the solar archives or reads local FITS files, displays and processes them, measures eruptions and their kinematics, and models the coronal magnetic field. Open it with Analysis > Solar Image Analysis in the main window.

This chapter describes the window, its menus and sessions, and how image data are obtained. Display and processing are described in Chapter 17, measurements in Chapter 18 and magnetic-field modeling in Chapter 19.

Supported observables

Table 16.1 lists the observables that can be retrieved. Local FITS files from these and other solar instruments can be loaded as well.

Observables available in Solar Image Analysis.
Instrument Class Observables
SDO/AIA (Lemen et al. 2012) EUV/UV disk 94, 131, 171, 193, 211, 304, 335, 1600 and 1700 Å
SDO/HMI (Scherrer et al. 2012) Magnetograph Magnetogram, Continuum (Intensitygram), Dopplergram; vector field (Section 17.10)
SOHO/EIT EUV disk 171, 195, 284 and 304 Å
SOHO/LASCO (Brueckner et al. 1995) Coronagraph C2, C3
STEREO-A/B SECCHI (Howard et al. 2008) EUV disk, coronagraph, heliospheric imager EUVI 171, 195, 284 and 304 Å; COR1, COR2; HI1, HI2
GOES/SUVI EUV disk 94, 131, 171, 195, 284 and 304 Å

The sidebar shows only the tool groups that apply to the instrument class of the loaded data (or, before loading, of the selected observable); see Table 16.4.

Window layout

The window is divided into the regions numbered in Figure 16.1 and described in Table 16.2.

Regions of the Solar Image Analysis window.
No. Region Description
1 Menu bar Session, Data, Analysis, Movie, Export and About (Section 16.2.1).
2 Sidebar Collapsible cards that read from top to bottom as the workflow: get data, choose records, analyze, then display, export and instrument-specific tools.
3 Sidebar handle Hides or shows the sidebar.
4 Header bar Live cursor readout — distance from Sun center in R⊙R_\odot, position angle, heliographic coordinates on the disk, and pixel — and the one-click Export MP4 button.
5 Measure toolbar The Measurements switch, the Ruler, Profile, Region Stats, Track CME, Circle Fit and Clear tools, and Pan / Zoom (Chapter 18).
6 Image canvas The current frame, titled with instrument, wavelength and time.
7 CME tracking panel Measurement table, live height–time graph and kinematic fit; active when Measurements is ticked (Section 18.4).
8 Playback bar Rewind, previous, play, pause and next buttons, the frame scrubber, the frame counter (Frame n / N) and the Speed in frames per second.
9 Details drawer Results and warnings of every operation. Click Details to collapse it; drag the divider above it to resize.

The playback speed set in the playback bar is used for playback and for exported movies. While a sequence plays, or while a contrast slider is dragged, the canvas switches to a fast preview that subsamples the display; full resolution returns as soon as playback stops. Measurements, statistics and exports always use the full-resolution data.

Menus

Menus of the Solar Image Analysis window.
Command Function
Session > Open Session… Open an .ecsolar session (Section 16.4).
Session > Save Session / Save Session As… Save the session (Ctrl+S / Ctrl+Shift+S).
Data > Fetch Archive Records Search the archive (Fetch Records).
Data > Find Latest Available Find the newest available data (Find Latest).
Data > SOHO Live Preview (Helioviewer) Near-real-time SOHO quicklook images (Section 16.3.3).
Data > Load Selected (to cache) Download and load the ticked records.
Data > Save Selected to Disk… Download the ticked records to a folder.
Data > Upload FITS Files Load local FITS files.
Data > Use Analyzer Window Copy the time range of the main window’s spectrum.
Data > Stop Download/Search Cancel the running operation.
Data > Reset All (clear cache & defaults) Clear the cache and restore default settings.
Analysis > Plot Frames, Running Difference, Composite Display modes (Section 17.1).
Analysis > Identify Active Regions, Fetch NOAA/HEK Labels Active-region tools (Section 17.5).
Analysis > Compare Viewpoint… Compare with a second observer (Section 17.6).
Analysis > GCS CME Fitting… Open GCS fitting at the time of the displayed frame (Chapter 20).
Analysis > Reset Loaded Frames Restore the frames as loaded.
Movie > Rewind, Back, Play, Pause, Forward Playback.
Movie > Build Movie Export a movie (Section 17.11).
Export > Export Plot, Export Cropped FITS, Export Regions CSV, Export MP4 Exports (Section 17.11).
About > About Solar Image Analysis… Version information.

Sidebar cards

Table 16.4 lists the sidebar cards in order, and the instrument classes for which each is shown.

Sidebar cards of Solar Image Analysis.
Card Shown for See
Data Source all Section 16.3.1
Archive Results all Section 16.3.2
Analysis all (disk tools for disk imagers and magnetographs only) Section 17.1
Processing Level AIA and SUVI Section 16.3.4
Display & Crop all Section 17.2
Solar Derotation all Section 17.3
Movie Export all Section 17.11
Coronagraph Tools coronagraphs Section 17.7
Overlay Layers coronagraphs Section 17.8
Heliospheric Imager (J-map) HI1, HI2 Section 17.9
Magnetic Vector Field (HMI) HMI Section 17.10
Potential Field (PFSS) disk imagers, magnetographs, synoptic maps Chapter 19
Active Regions disk imagers, magnetographs Section 17.5

Obtaining image data

The Data Source card

The Data Source card (Figure 16.2) defines what to retrieve and how.

Observable

the instrument and wavelength or product (Table 16.1).

Start (UTC), End (UTC)

the time range.

Cadence (s)

the sampling interval between frames (0–3600 s; default 120 s).

Max records

the maximum number of records to list (1–5000; default 120).

Use Analyzer Time Window

copies the start and end times of the spectrum in the main window, so that the images match the radio burst being studied.

Download options (SDO)
Source

Auto (JSOC → VSO) tries the Joint Science Operations Center (JSOC) first and falls back to the Virtual Solar Observatory (VSO); JSOC (fast) returns direct, compressed AIA files and is usually much faster; VSO (classic) uses the VSO only.

JSOC notify e-mail

JSOC requires a one-time, free registration of an e-mail address at https://jsoc.stanford.edu/ajax/register_email.html. The address is remembered.

Frame size

Full disk (4096²), Binned ½ (2048²), Binned ¼ (1024²) or Cutout (region). Binned and cutout frames are produced by JSOC, so only the reduced data are transferred; they require the JSOC source and e-mail. For a cutout, enter the Centre X″, Centre Y″, Width″ and Height″ in arcseconds from disk center.

High resolution AIA (best crop)

requests full-resolution AIA products. Files are larger, but cropped views keep more detail.

An estimate of the download size is shown below the options when records are selected.

Actions
Fetch Records

searches the archive; the matching records appear in Archive Results. Stop cancels a running search or download; files already completed remain in the cache.

Find Latest

scans the archive backwards to find the newest data actually available for the observable. This is useful for SOHO/LASCO, whose calibrated archive can lag real time by many months, and may take a minute or two.

Upload FITS…

loads solar FITS files from disk without an archive search.

Live Preview (Helioviewer)

shown for SOHO/LASCO and SOHO/EIT (Section 16.3.3).

The Archive Results card

The Archive Results table lists the records found, with the columns Use, Start UTC, Source, Size and File ID. Tick records in the Use column, or use Select All and Deselect All, then:

  • Load Selected downloads the ticked records into the working cache and loads them for analysis; or

  • Save to Disk… downloads them to a folder you choose, for keeping.

The Analysis card then summarizes what is loaded (instrument, number of frames and configuration).

SOHO data

The archive serves two files for every SOHO/EIT observation, the calibrated Level 1 file and the raw level-zero file. The window chooses one per observation: Level 1 where it exists and the raw file otherwise. Level 1 processing runs about a year behind the raw archive, so recent searches return raw frames and older ones calibrated frames; a window that straddles the boundary loads as two configuration groups. The calibrated SOHO/LASCO archive also lags real time. For a date beyond the newest archived data, the search falls back to the nearest available data and says so. Use Live Preview to see the most recent SOHO images.

Live Preview (Helioviewer)

Live Preview (Helioviewer) opens the SOHO/… Near-Real-Time Preview (Helioviewer) window (Figure 16.3) with the newest quicklook image of SOHO/LASCO C2 or C3 or SOHO/EIT, usually updated within about an hour. These browse images are for situational awareness, not for analysis.

Passband / Detector, Latest Frame

choose the EIT passband or LASCO detector, and reload the newest image.

Movie (time range · step)

set Start (UTC), End (UTC), Step (minutes) and Max frames, then Build Movie to fetch one frame per step and play them with ◀, Play, Pause, ▶ and an FPS setting. Cancel stops the fetch. The frame cap protects the Helioviewer service.

Open in Browser

opens the view on the Helioviewer web site.

Processing level

Downloads always fetch the archive’s base product. For instruments that publish more than one processing level, the Processing Level card selects the level that is displayed and analyzed:

SDO/AIA

Level 1 (as downloaded), the archive product; or Level 1.5 (registered here), computed locally with aiapy (Barnes et al. 2020), which applies the master pointing, rotates the image to solar north, rescales it to 0.6 arcsec per pixel and centers the Sun.

GOES/SUVI

Level 1b (as downloaded), single calibrated exposures; or Level 2 (archive composite), NOAA’s high-dynamic-range composites, which are downloaded separately when selected.

Apply Level re-derives the loaded sequence at the selected level; any crop or derotation is re-applied afterwards. The status line reports the level in use. The card is hidden for instruments that offer only one level.

Sessions

A Solar Image Analysis session (.ecsolar) is a single file that reopens an analysis exactly where it was left. It embeds the original FITS frames, so it survives a cleared cache or a move to another computer (at the cost of a large file), together with the data source, the display, crop and playback state, the CME measurements (height–time picks, circle fits and fit order) and the PFSS settings. The PFSS solution itself is not stored; one click on Compute PFSS reproduces it. Sessions are opened and saved from the Session menu (Ctrl+S, Ctrl+Shift+S).

Level 1 processing runs about a year behind the raw archive, so recent searches return raw frames and older ones calibrated frames; a window that straddles the boundary loads as two configuration groups. The calibrated SOHO/LASCO archive also lags real time. For a date beyond the newest archived data, the search falls back to the nearest available data and says so. Use Live Preview to see the most recent SOHO images. Live Preview (Helioviewer) Live Preview (Helioviewer) opens the SOHO/… Near-Real-Time Preview (Helioviewer) window (Figure 16.3 ) with the newest quicklook image of SOHO/LASCO C2 or C3 or SOHO/EIT, usually updated within about an hour. These browse images are for situational awareness, not for analysis. Figure 16.3. The SOHO near-real-time preview. View illustration in the PDF edition. Passband / Detector, Latest Frame choose the EIT passband or LASCO detector, and reload the newest image. Movie (time range · step) set Start (UTC) , End (UTC) , Step (minutes) and Max frames , then Build Movie to fetch one frame per step and play them with ◀ , Play , Pause , ▶ and an FPS setting. Cancel stops the fetch. The frame cap protects the Helioviewer service. Open in Browser opens the view on the Helioviewer web site. Processing level Downloads always fetch the archive’s base product. For instruments that publish more than one processing level, the Processing Level card selects the level that is displayed and analyzed: SDO/AIA Level 1 (as downloaded) , the archive product; or Level 1.5 (registered here) , computed locally with aiapy ( Barnes et al. 2020 ) , which applies the master pointing, rotates the image to solar north, rescales it to 0.6 arcsec per pixel and centers the Sun. GOES/SUVI Level 1b (as downloaded) , single calibrated exposures; or Level 2 (archive composite) , NOAA’s high-dynamic-range composites, which are downloaded separately when selected. Apply Level re-derives the loaded sequence at the selected level; any crop or derotation is re-applied afterwards. The status line reports the level in use. The card is hidden for instruments that offer only one level. Sessions A Solar Image Analysis session ( .ecsolar ) is a single file that reopens an analysis exactly where it was left. It embeds the original FITS frames, so it survives a cleared cache or a move to another computer (at the cost of a large file), together with the data source, the display, crop and playback state, the CME measurements (height–time picks, circle fits and fit order) and the PFSS settings. The PFSS solution itself is not stored; one click on Compute PFSS reproduces it. Sessions are opened and saved from the Session menu ( Ctrl+S , Ctrl+Shift+S ).

title: Image Display and Processing
html:
Image Display and Processing

This chapter describes the tools of Solar Image Analysis that display, enhance, combine and export image sequences once they are loaded (Chapter 16).

The Analysis card

The Analysis card (Figure 17.1a) shows a summary of the loaded data and the main display modes and analysis tools.

Plot Frames

displays the loaded sequence as plain frames.

Running Diff

displays each frame minus the previous one, which makes moving and changing features stand out.

Base Diff

displays each frame minus the first, showing the total change since the start — useful for eruptions, coronal dimmings and EUV waves.

Composite

builds an RGB tri-color image from the first three AIA frames or, when a magnetogram overlay has been loaded, draws HMI polarity contours on the current AIA frame (red positive, blue negative).

Mag Overlay…

loads an HMI magnetogram FITS file for the composite; the box beside it sets the contour level (10–2000 G; default 100 G).

Light Curve

plots the mean intensity of a region against time (Section 17.4).

Active Regions

, NOAA/HEK Labels detect and label active regions (Section 17.5).

Compare Viewpoint…

compares the frame with a second observer (Section 17.6).

Reset Frames

restores the frames as downloaded, discarding crops, processing levels, derotation, composites and detected regions.

Composite, Mag Overlay…, Active Regions and NOAA/HEK Labels are available only for disk imagers and magnetographs. The difference modes also determine the content of exported movies (Section 17.11).

Display and cropping

The Display & Crop card (Figure 17.1b) controls the appearance of the image:

Renderer

PyQtGraph (default; fast, and required for clicked PFSS seeds and the interactive crop rectangle) or Matplotlib.

Colormap

instrument color maps (for example sdoaia193, hmimag, soholasco2, stereocor2, euvi195, goes-rsuvi171) and general ones (inferno, magma, plasma, viridis, cividis, gray, RdBu_r, hot). A suitable map is chosen automatically for each observable.

Scale

linear or log.

Clip low, Clip high

the lower and upper percentiles mapped to the ends of the color scale (defaults 1% and 99.9%); dragging gives a live preview.

Solar Limb

draws the photospheric limb.

Coordinate Grid, Grid frame

overlays a graticule of meridians and parallels in the selected frame — Heliocentric Inertial (HCI, the default), Stonyhurst or Carrington. The same frame is used for the heliographic coordinates of the cursor readout.

Colorbar, Region Overlays

show the color bar and the detected active regions.

Cropping

Under Crop (arcsec), enter X min / max and Y min / max in arcseconds from disk center, or tick Rectangle crop to drag a rectangle on the image that fills in the fields. Apply Crop crops all loaded frames to the rectangle. Cropping is done locally after the files are loaded. Export Cropped FITS saves the cropped frames as FITS files with updated coordinate metadata.

The crop rectangle also defines the region used by Region Stats, the light curve, the derotation and the Current crop PFSS seeding.

Solar derotation

Over a sequence of several hours, a fixed rectangle slowly drifts onto neighboring surface because of solar differential rotation. The Solar Derotation card keeps a selected region on the same piece of the Sun:

Derotate selected area

enables derotation of the crop region.

Mode

Track region (no resampling) moves the cut-out window with the rotation and keeps the original pixel values, so it is the mode for photometry and light curves. Reproject to reference time resamples every frame onto the reference time’s grid, which corrects foreshortening and gives all frames one coordinate system, making differencing meaningful, at the cost of interpolating the data.

Reference

First frame, Current frame or Specific frame... (with its number): the frame from which the region is read and to whose time every other frame is rotated.

Padding

the extra margin cut around the region before reprojecting (0–600 arcsec; default 60 arcsec), so that the interpolation has data up to the edge. Reproject mode only.

Apply Derotation, Reset to Full Frames

apply the derotation, or discard the cut-out and restore the full frames at the current processing level.

The status line reports whether derotation is active.

Region light curve

Light Curve plots the mean intensity of the crop region (or of the whole frame if Rectangle crop is off), converted to DN/s using the exposure time, against time (Figure 17.2). The time of peak intensity is marked and, when a spectrum is loaded in the main window, its time window is shaded so that the EUV brightening can be timed against the radio burst. At least two frames are needed.

Active regions

The Active Regions card detects bright regions in the current frame and lists them:

Threshold

the intensity percentile above which pixels count as bright (50–100; default 98).

Min px

the minimum area of a region in pixels (default 12).

Region table

one row per region with ID, Label, NOAA number, Centroid, Area, Peak intensity and Source.

Click Active Regions in the Analysis card to run the detection, and NOAA/HEK Labels to fetch the NOAA active-region numbers from the Heliophysics Event Knowledge base (HEK) and attach them to the detected regions; the status line reports whether metadata are loaded. Detected regions are drawn on the image when Region Overlays is ticked. Export Regions CSV saves the table with centroids, bounding boxes and intensities. Detection works on local files; the labels need network access.

Comparing viewpoints

Compare Viewpoint… opens a window that compares the current frame (viewpoint A) with a second observable (viewpoint B) taken near the same time — for example a STEREO image against the Earth view.

  1. Choose the Second viewpoint observable and the search window (±, 1–720 min; default 30 min).

  2. Click Fetch Viewpoint B. Viewpoint B is downloaded, reprojected onto the coordinate frame of A, and shown beside it.

  3. Tick Blink to alternate between the two images in place.

The Observer separation line gives the angle between the two observers.

Coronagraph tools

For coronagraph data the Coronagraph Tools card offers NRGF radial filter, the normalizing-radial-graded filter (Morgan et al. 2006). It flattens the steep radial fall-off of coronal brightness so that faint CME fronts become visible at all heights. It applies to the plain frame view; difference images already remove the background.

Overlay layers

A CME is never fully visible in one instrument: the eruption starts on the disk (AIA, EIT, EUVI), crosses the low corona (LASCO C2, COR1) and expands into the outer corona (LASCO C3, COR2), and each coronagraph is blind inside its occulter. For coronagraph views the Overlay Layers card blends several instruments into one continuous image from the disk to the outer corona.

Add, Remove

choose an observable and add it to the layer list, or remove the selected layer. Layers are painted widest field of view first. Untick a layer to leave it out without losing its settings.

Per-layer settings

for the selected layer: Colormap, Scale (log or linear), Opacity, Midtones (gamma; 50 suits most solar images), and the Inner and Outer edges of its field of view in R⊙R_\odot. Pixels inside the inner edge stay transparent so that the layer below shows through.

Time match

how far from each loaded frame’s time a layer frame may be taken (1–720 min; default 30 min). Widen it for slow cadences or patchy archives.

Build Composite

downloads each layer’s matching frames, reprojects them onto the loaded series and blends them, in the background with a progress bar. The result replaces the view and works with the measurement tools, plot export and movie export.

Clear

drops the composite and restores the originally loaded frames.

Note

Each layer is color-mapped before blending, because EUV disk images and the white-light corona differ by orders of magnitude. Coronagraph layers are reprojected under a spherical-screen assumption, flagged as approximate in the build notes: cross-observer coronagraph overlays are morphological context, not photometry. SOHO/LASCO files carry no observer position, so an Earth-based observer is assumed (accurate to about 1%).

Heliospheric imager J-maps

For STEREO HI1 and HI2 data the Heliospheric Imager (J-map) card builds a time–elongation map (Sheeley et al. 1999):

Background

Median background removes the static F-corona and star field with the per-pixel temporal median; Previous frame uses a running difference.

PA

the position angle of the slit, counter-clockwise from the image +x+x axis (90° points up; default 90°). Set it along the CME direction.

Build J-map

stacks the slit profiles of all frames into the HI J-map window (elongation in degrees against frame index). An outward-moving CME appears as a slanted bright track.

HMI vector magnetic field

For SDO/HMI data the Magnetic Vector Field (HMI) card overlays the measured photospheric vector field:

Load Vector FITS…

loads the hmi.B_720s field, inclination and azimuth segments of each time step from disk (with the optional disambiguation segment, applied automatically).

Download Vector (JSOC)

downloads hmi.B_720s for the query time window through JSOC; this needs the registered JSOC e-mail. Each 720-s time step is four segments of about 50 MB. If no HMI image is loaded, the derived vertical-field (BzB_z) magnetogram is plotted with the vectors.

Show vector field

overlays the field on the HMI frame. The transverse component is drawn as Arrows (length proportional to strength) and/or Streamlines, and |B| layer tints the image by total field strength. Arrows are red where the vertical field points toward the observer (+Bz+B_z) and blue where it points away.

Spacing, Threshold

the arrow grid spacing (16–512 detector pixels; default 64) and the minimum transverse field drawn (50–2000 G; default 200 G). The transverse noise floor of hmi.B_720s is about 100 G.

Movies and still images

Movie Export card

choose the Content (Frames, Running Difference or Base Difference) and the Format (MP4 or GIF), and click Build Movie…. Movies use the playback speed set under the viewer and the current color map, scale, clipping and crop.

Export MP4

in the header bar makes a one-click MP4 of the loaded sequence with the current display settings.

Export Plot

saves the current frame, with its overlays, as an image.

Export Cropped FITS

saves the cropped frames as FITS files.

Export Regions CSV

saves the active-region table.

The same exports are available from the Export and Movie menus.

title: Measurements and CME Kinematics

headings.title: Fitting a circle to a CME front

html:
Measurements and CME Kinematics

The Measure toolbar above the image provides click-driven tools for distances, intensity profiles, region statistics and CME tracking. The CME tracking panel to the right of the image collects the measurements of a sequence and fits their kinematics.

Enabling the tools

Tick Measurements in the Measure toolbar to enable the tools; the CME tracking panel becomes available at the same time. One tool is active at a time. A right-click or Esc cancels a pick in progress without leaving the tool. Results are shown in the status line and appended to the Details drawer. Pan / Zoom, at the right of the toolbar, enables dragging and scroll-wheel zooming of the image; the zoom is kept while the movie plays, and unticking it returns to the full frame.

Tools of the Measure toolbar.
Tool What it does
Ruler Two clicks give the plane-of-sky distance in arcseconds, R⊙R_\odot and Mm, and the position angle (measured from north toward east).
Profile Two clicks plot the intensity along the cut, for example across a loop, a filament or a CME front, in the Intensity Profile window.
Region Stats Summarizes the crop rectangle: pixel count, mean, median, minimum, maximum, standard deviation and intensity-weighted centroid (arcsec). Enable Rectangle crop first to choose the region.
Track CME One click per frame on the leading edge of a CME. The height is its distance from disk center. Best for limb events.
Circle Fit Three or more clicks along a circular front per frame. Best for eruptions near disk center.
Clear Resets every measurement: picks, circles, table and overlays.

The 3-D reconstruction of CMEs from several viewpoints is performed in the separate GCS CME Fitting window (Part VI), opened from Analysis > GCS CME Fitting….

Tracking a CME

Track CME measures a height–time profile with one click per frame (Figure 18.1).

  1. Go to the first frame in which the CME front is visible.

  2. Select Track CME and click the leading edge. The pick is added to the tracking table and, with Auto-advance frame after each pick ticked (the default), the next frame is shown.

  3. Repeat on each frame, then choose the fit order and click Fit Height–Time.

The height is the plane-of-sky distance of the clicked point from Sun center in R⊙R_\odot; the position angle (PA) is recorded with it. The tool works on any imager — EUVI, AIA, SUVI, COR, LASCO and HI. Clicking again on a frame replaces its pick.

Fitting a circle to a CME front

For eruptions near disk center the front expands as a growing dome rather than moving outwards from the limb, and a single leading-edge click has no well-defined origin. Circle Fit models the CME as a uniformly expanding sphere resting on the solar surface (Figure 18.2).

  1. Select Circle Fit and click three or more points along the visible front. The least-squares circle is drawn from the third click and tightens with each further point.

  2. Click Commit Circle (Ctrl+Return). The frame’s result is added to the table and the next frame is shown.

  3. Repeat on each frame, then click Fit Height–Time.

Each row gives the height h=1R⊙+2rh = 1\,R_\odot + 2r, where rr is the fitted radius (the sphere’s top is one diameter above the surface), the radius in R⊙R_\odot, the position angle of the center and the number of points. The fit residual, the center and the leading-edge distance from disk center appear in the row’s tooltip. Re-committing a frame replaces its entry.

  • Click a wide arc. A short arc is fitted, but it constrains the radius very weakly, and the panel warns when the arc spans less than about 30°.

  • Lock centre freezes the center at its current fitted value so that later frames fit the radius alone. Use it once the dome has stopped drifting.

The fit uses Taubin’s method (Taubin 1991), which is not biased toward small radii on partial arcs, and works in helioprojective arcseconds so that the front remains a circle when the plate scale differs between the axes.

The CME tracking panel

The tracking panel shows the measurements of the active tool:

Table

for Track CME: Time (UT), t (s) since the first pick, Height (R☉) and PA (°); for Circle Fit: additionally Radius (R☉) and the number of points N.

Height–time graph

the measured heights against time, with the live fit.

Fit

the polynomial order: Linear, Quadratic or Cubic. Changing it refits the points already in the graph.

Fit Height–Time

fits the points and reports the speed and acceleration below the graph.

Clear Picks / Clear Circles

removes the measurements of the active tool.

Export

Table as CSV…, or Graph (PNG, PDF, EPS, SVG, TIFF, JPG)… drawn in light mode and the OriginPro style.

Background: height–time fits

Linear

h=h0+vth = h_0 + v t: one plane-of-sky speed for the whole track. The acceleration is taken from a companion quadratic fit, as in the CDAW CME catalog.

Quadratic

h=h0+v0t+12at2h = h_0 + v_0 t + \tfrac12 a t^2: constant acceleration, with the speed reported at the first and last frame.

Cubic

adds a constant jerk, with the speed and acceleration reported at both ends.

Every value carries a 1σ1\sigma uncertainty propagated from the fit covariance, so the correlations between the polynomial terms are included. A fit of degree nn needs n+1n+1 points, and n+2n+2 before an uncertainty can be estimated; with fewer points the value is shown without an error rather than with a misleading zero. Heights from Track CME are plane-of-sky distances, so the derived speeds generally underestimate the true radial speed; Circle Fit heights rely on the assumption of a sphere expanding from the surface.

The measurements — picks, circles, the lock state and the fit order — are saved in .ecsolar sessions (Section 16.4).

Fitting a circle to a CME front For eruptions near disk center the front expands as a growing dome rather than moving outwards from the limb, and a single leading-edge click has no well-defined origin. Circle Fit models the CME as a uniformly expanding sphere resting on the solar surface (Figure 18.2 ). Select Circle Fit and click three or more points along the visible front. The least-squares circle is drawn from the third click and tightens with each further point. Click Commit Circle ( Ctrl+Return ). The frame’s result is added to the table and the next frame is shown. Repeat on each frame, then click Fit Height–Time . Each row gives the height h = 1 R ⊙ + 2 r , where r is the fitted radius (the sphere’s top is one diameter above the surface), the radius in R ⊙ , the position angle of the center and the number of points. The fit residual, the center and the leading-edge distance from disk center appear in the row’s tooltip. Re-committing a frame replaces its entry. Click a wide arc. A short arc is fitted, but it constrains the radius very weakly, and the panel warns when the arc spans less than about 30°. Lock centre freezes the center at its current fitted value so that later frames fit the radius alone. Use it once the dome has stopped drifting. The fit uses Taubin’s method ( Taubin 1991 ) , which is not biased toward small radii on partial arcs, and works in helioprojective arcseconds so that the front remains a circle when the plate scale differs between the axes. Figure 18.2. Circle fitting of an on-disk CME front. View illustration in the PDF edition. The CME tracking panel The tracking panel shows the measurements of the active tool: Table for Track CME : Time (UT) , t (s) since the first pick, Height (R☉) and PA (°) ; for Circle Fit : additionally Radius (R☉) and the number of points N . Height–time graph the measured heights against time, with the live fit. Fit the polynomial order: Linear , Quadratic or Cubic . Changing it refits the points already in the graph. Fit Height–Time fits the points and reports the speed and acceleration below the graph. Clear Picks / Clear Circles removes the measurements of the active tool. Export Table as CSV… , or Graph (PNG, PDF, EPS, SVG, TIFF, JPG)… drawn in light mode and the OriginPro style. Background: height–time fits Linear h = h 0 + v t : one plane-of-sky speed for the whole track. The acceleration is taken from a companion quadratic fit, as in the CDAW CME catalog. Quadratic h = h 0 + v 0 t + 1 2 a t 2 : constant acceleration, with the speed reported at the first and last frame. Cubic adds a constant jerk, with the speed and acceleration reported at both ends. Every value carries a 1 σ uncertainty propagated from the fit covariance, so the correlations between the polynomial terms are included. A fit of degree n needs n + 1 points, and n + 2 before an uncertainty can be estimated; with fewer points the value is shown without an error rather than with a misleading zero. Heights from Track CME are plane-of-sky distances, so the derived speeds generally underestimate the true radial speed; Circle Fit heights rely on the assumption of a sphere expanding from the surface. The measurements — picks, circles, the lock state and the fit order — are saved in .ecsolar sessions (Section 16.4 ).

title: Coronal Magnetic Field Modeling (PFSS)
html:
Coronal Magnetic Field Modeling (PFSS)

An EUV image shows where the coronal plasma is, not where the magnetic field is. The Potential Field (PFSS) card of Solar Image Analysis extrapolates the coronal magnetic field from a photospheric magnetogram with the potential-field source-surface model (Schatten et al. 1969; Altschuler and Newkirk 1969) and draws the resulting field lines over the disk (Figure 19.1), so that the modeled loop topology and coronal holes can be compared with the image. The card is shown for disk imagers, magnetographs and synoptic maps.

Background: the PFSS model

The model assumes a current-free (potential) field between the photosphere and a spherical source surface a few solar radii out, where the field is forced to be radial to mimic the solar wind dragging it open. Field lines that reach the source surface are open and feed the solar wind; the others are closed loops. The open-field footpoint regions are the model’s coronal holes, and the polarity-inversion line on the source surface marks where the heliospheric current sheet leaves the model.

Caution

AIA images carry no magnetic-field information, so the boundary condition comes from a synoptic magnetogram — a full-Sun map assembled from central-meridian observations over a whole solar rotation. The model therefore describes the global field around your observation, never the instantaneous field, and the far side is always at least two weeks old. The card shows how far the map’s date is from the displayed frame; that offset is the number to judge the result by.

Settings

Settings of the Potential Field (PFSS) card.
Setting Description
Magnetogram The boundary condition (Section 19.1.1). For GONG ADAPT, Realization (0–11) chooses one of the twelve flux-transport realizations; for Local FITS file..., Browse… selects the file. The line below names the loaded map and its time offset from the frame.
Source surface Height at which the field is forced radial (1.5–10 R⊙R_\odot; default 2.5 R⊙R_\odot). Lowering it opens more field.
Radial cells Radial grid resolution between the photosphere and the source surface (10–150; default 35). More is smoother and slower.
Seeds Where field lines start (Section 19.1.2).
Density Seed density (4–64; default 12, about 150 field lines). It controls both speed and legibility; the hint beside it estimates the number of lines.

Magnetograms

GONG synoptic

the ground-based GONG synoptic map (Harvey et al. 1996), updated daily and available for any date from 2006 on. No registration is needed; this is the usual choice.

HMI synoptic (JSOC)

SDO’s own synoptic map, instrumentally consistent with AIA. Searching is free, but downloading stages a JSOC export and needs the registered e-mail set in the Data Source card. The series is published about one Carrington rotation behind, so the most recent weeks are not covered.

GONG ADAPT

maps from the ADAPT flux-transport model, which estimates the unobserved far side instead of leaving it weeks old and usually improves open-field predictions. One file holds twelve realizations, which differ mostly on the far side.

Local FITS file...

a synoptic map you already have. It must be a full-Sun Carrington map; plate-carrée maps are reprojected to equal-area automatically.

Downloaded magnetograms are cached, so changing a model parameter and solving again does not download the map again. Unmeasured pixels, such as the polar gaps in GONG maps, are filled with zero so that the solution can be computed; their number is reported.

Seeds

Uniform grid

an equal-area sample over the visible hemisphere.

Open-field regions

a coarse survey is traced first, and then lines are started only where the field is open. This shows coronal-hole connectivity without closed loops dominating the picture.

Current crop

concentrates the lines inside the crop rectangle.

Clicked points

traces one line from each point clicked on the disk. This needs the PyQtGraph renderer.

Tracing costs about 1.6 ms per field line, so a solution takes a few seconds at most, but beyond about 150 lines the field lines start to hide the image they are compared with. Prefer Open-field regions to a high density when coronal-hole connectivity is what you want.

Computing and displaying the model

Compute PFSS downloads the magnetogram if needed, solves the potential field and traces the field lines in the background; Clear removes the overlay and the solution. The Show options toggle the layers without recomputing:

Open field

lines reaching the source surface, colored by the sign of the radial field at their footpoint: red outward, blue inward.

Closed loops

lines returning to the photosphere, drawn in gray.

Open-field boundaries

outlines of the open-field footpoint regions, for comparison with the dark coronal holes in 193 or 211 Å images.

Near side only

(on by default) hides lines rooted on the far hemisphere. Such lines are not hidden behind the disk once they rise above the limb, so they would otherwise be drawn as arcs outside the disk with no visible footpoint. Clear it for the geometrically complete picture.

Stepping through a sequence re-projects the same solution onto each frame instead of solving again. This is correct, because the synoptic map is valid across the rotation while the observer’s view changes from frame to frame.

Diagnostics

Diagnostics… opens a four-panel window that documents the solution (Figure 19.2):

  1. the input magnetogram (BrB_r) with its provenance;

  2. the radial field at the source surface with its neutral line, where the heliospheric current sheet leaves the model — the model’s most directly testable prediction;

  3. the open (red and blue) and closed (dark) footpoint map in Carrington projection;

  4. the solution statistics, including the open flux, the open-area fraction and the number of filled pixels.

Save Figure… saves all four panels as one image (PNG, PDF or SVG).

Note

PFSS modeling uses the sunkit-magex package (Stansby et al. 2020), which is included in the installers. When the application is run from source without it, the card remains visible but disabled and shows the command to install it. Sessions store the PFSS settings, not the solution (Section 16.4).

title: The GCS CME Fitting Window
html:
The GCS CME Fitting Window

A single coronagraph view cannot separate a CME’s direction from its size: a wide CME aimed at the observer and a narrow one crossing the sky can look alike. Two well-separated views break that ambiguity, and a third over-constrains it. The GCS CME Fitting window reconstructs a CME in three dimensions by fitting one Graduated Cylindrical Shell (GCS) model (Thernisien et al. 2006; Thernisien 2011) to up to three coronagraph viewpoints at once, and optionally a spheroid or ellipsoid to the shock the CME drives (Kouloumvakos et al. 2019; Kwon et al. 2014). The parameters follow the conventions of PyThea (Kouloumvakos et al. 2022), so results can be compared directly.

This chapter describes the window and how images are loaded and viewed. Fitting, recording and exporting are described in Chapter 21.

Opening the window

Open the window with Analysis > GCS CME Fitting… in the main window or in Solar Image Analysis. The window downloads its own images, so nothing needs to be loaded first:

  • from the main window, the visible time range of the spectrum becomes the event range;

  • from Solar Image Analysis, the event range is centered on the displayed frame, one hour either side.

Choosing the menu item again reuses the open window and passes it the new time.

Window layout

The window is divided into the regions numbered in Figure 20.1 and described in Table 20.1.

Regions of the GCS CME Fitting window.
No. Region Description
1 Menu bar File, Event, View, Fit and Help (Section 20.7).
2 Toolbar Playback, the shared time, image mode, layout and overlay toggles (Section 20.3).
3 Viewpoint panels Panels A, B and C, each showing one channel’s image nearest the shared time, with the models drawn on it.
4 Event & channels card Event range, frame cap, time-offset limit and the three channels (Section 20.4).
5 Model card The edited model, its parameters, front-point controls, Refine fit and Commit (Chapter 21).
6 Display card Wireframe colors and style, and each image’s color map and contrast (Section 20.6).
7 Kinematics card Recorded fits, height–time graph and fit (Section 21.6).
8 Status bar Messages, including the views taking part in a fit and their separations, and the helioprojective position under the cursor.

Toolbar

Playback

first frame (Home), previous (←), play and pause (Space), next (→), and the playback speed (1–30 fps; default 4 fps). With fits recorded, the model follows them during playback.

Time slider and time label

step through the event. Every panel shows its own image nearest the selected UTC time, which is displayed beside the slider.

View

Raw (the images as downloaded), Running diff (each image minus the previous one; selected whenever images load) or Base diff (each image minus the first of the sequence).

Layout

Equal shows three equal images with the cards beneath (0); A, B or C enlarges that panel, stacks the other two beside it and moves the cards to the right (1–3).

Solar limb, Axes, Banner

outline the photosphere in every image (on by default; the reference against which a CME’s height is judged), show arcsecond axes around each image, and show the information banner across the top of each image (B).

The keys apply while an image has keyboard focus.

Loading the viewpoints

The Event & channels (UTC) card (Figure 20.2) defines what is loaded.

Event

the UTC start and end of the event, up to three days. Changing them sets every channel’s range; each channel’s range can then be adjusted on its own.

≤\leq frames

the maximum number of images per channel (2–200; default 60). A longer sequence is thinned evenly across the event rather than cut short.

Load all

(Ctrl+L) loads every channel. Each channel also has its own Load button and a frame count. Event > Cancel downloads stops a slow load.

Max time offset

the largest difference between an image’s time and the shared time for the image to take part in a fit (0–60 min; default 5 min). Models are still drawn on the other panels for comparison. Use a smaller value for a fast-evolving CME; the default is a workflow choice, not an accuracy guarantee.

A, B, C

the channel of each panel and its time range.

The available channels are listed in Table 20.2. By default panels A, B and C show STEREO-B COR2, SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO-A COR2, left to right. Channels without data for the event date are grayed out. The STEREO-B archive ends on 27 September 2014, so for later events panel A reports that it has no data; only SOHO and STEREO-A then remain as vantage points, and another channel in panel A (LASCO C3 or COR1-A) adds an image but not a new viewing direction.

Coronagraph channels available for GCS fitting.
Channel Available
SOHO LASCO C2 from 21 February 1997
SOHO LASCO C3 from 20 February 1997
STEREO-A COR1 from 4 December 2006
STEREO-A COR2 from 29 December 2006
STEREO-B COR1 12 December 2006 to 27 September 2014
STEREO-B COR2 10 January 2007 to 27 September 2014

The images are Helioviewer JPEG2000 files, so loading needs network access; downloaded images are cached and reused. Changing a channel’s source or range discards its loaded images and any pending results. A 15-minute e-CALLISTO file spans only one or two coronagraph images (about one every 15 minutes for COR2 and every 12 minutes for LASCO C2), so widen the range to follow a CME.

Reading the images

The banner across each image gives the instrument, the actual observation time, its offset from the shared time and the difference reference. In running difference the first image of each channel is differenced against the archive image just before the range, and is shown raw only when no earlier image exists. Clicked front points belong to the image on which they were clicked and return when that image is shown again.

The Display card

Wireframe

GCS… and Shock… choose the colors of the two models (orange and sky blue by default); Width (0.5–8 px), Opacity (10–100%) and Density (mesh density, 1–8) set the wireframe style.

Image A, B, C

select a panel, then set its Colormap and contrast sliders. Every load resets the color map to gray.

Menus

Menus of the GCS CME Fitting window.
Command Function Shortcut
File > Export analysis JSON… Parameters, points and provenance of both models. Ctrl+Shift+S
File > Export recorded fits CSV… Recorded series of the edited model.
File > Export height–time graph… Height–time graph with the chosen fit.
File > Save viewpoint snapshot… The three views as shown.
File > Export movie (GIF/MP4)… Movie of the event with recorded shells.
File > Export fitting report (PDF)… Complete fitting report.
File > Close window Close the window. Ctrl+W
Event > Load all channels Load every channel. Ctrl+L
Event > Cancel downloads Stop running loads.
Event > Apply event range to all channels Reset every channel to the event range.
Event > Go to UTC time… Jump to the image nearest a typed time. Ctrl+G
Event > First / Previous / Next / Last frame, Play / pause Navigation and playback. Space
View > Raw / Running difference / Base difference Image mode.
View > Equal viewpoints / Focus A / Focus B / Focus C Layout. 0–3
View > GCS wireframe / Shock wireframe / Solar limb / Arcsecond axes / Image banners Overlay toggles. B
View > Reset image zoom, Fit layout to window Restore the zoom and the panel sizes.
Fit > Edit GCS flux rope / Edit shock Choose the model to edit.
Fit > Pick front points Toggle point picking.
Fit > Undo last front point Remove the last point clicked in any panel. Ctrl+Z
Fit > Clear current front points Remove the edited model’s points.
Fit > Refine current model Least-squares refinement. Ctrl+R
Fit > Record fit at current time Commit the fit. Ctrl+Return
Fit > Restore / Delete recorded fit at current time Revisit or remove a recorded fit.
Fit > Reset model parameters Reset the edited model.
Fit > Fit recorded heights over time Kinematic fit.
Help > Fitting workflow and scientific limits… Summary of the procedure and its limits. F1
