title: Fitting the Flux Rope and the Shock
html:
Fitting the Flux Rope and the Shock

This chapter describes the models of the GCS CME Fitting window, how they are aligned and refined against the observed fronts, how fits are recorded over time to build kinematics, and how results are exported.

The Model card

The Model card (Figure 21.1) shows the parameters of one model at a time. Choose the model with Edit on the card’s title row:

GCS flux rope

the Graduated Cylindrical Shell, fitted to the CME ejecta.

Shock

a spheroid or ellipsoid, fitted to the shock the CME drives — its faint outer envelope (Section 21.7).

Both models are drawn in every panel (the shell in orange and the shock in sky blue by default); the edited model is the one that the handles, clicks, Refine fit, Commit and the Kinematics card act on.

GCS parameters

Six sliders, each with a numeric entry, control the shell (Table 21.1).

Parameters of the GCS flux-rope model.
Slider Range Meaning
Lon −180∘-180^\circ to 180∘180^\circ Stonyhurst longitude of the direction of propagation.
Lat −89∘-89^\circ to 89∘89^\circ Stonyhurst latitude of the direction of propagation.
Tilt −90∘-90^\circ to 90∘90^\circ Rotation of the shell about the propagation direction.
Height 1.05–30 R⊙R_\odot Distance of the leading edge (apex) from Sun center — not the altitude above the surface.
α\alpha 1∘1^\circ–80∘80^\circ Half-angle between the legs of the shell.
κ\kappa 0.05–0.95 Aspect ratio, controlling the thickness of the shell.

Set the direction, tilt, α\alpha and κ\kappa before fine-tuning the height. The apex can also be dragged in any panel: moving it around the Sun turns the direction, and moving it outwards or inwards changes the height. The readout below the sliders gives the derived leg height, apex cross-section radius, center distance, and the intrinsic face-on and edge-on widths.

Background: GCS geometry

The GCS is a hollow croissant: two conical legs joined by a curved front with a circular cross-section that grows with distance from the Sun (Thernisien et al. 2006; Thernisien 2011). The face-on width is 2[α+arcsin⁡κ]2[\alpha + \arcsin\kappa] and the edge-on width 2arcsin⁡κ2\arcsin\kappa; both include the shell thickness and differ from the apparent width in a coronagraph image. Because the height is the leading edge, it feeds the height–time fit directly. GCS is a flux-rope model, not a shock model.

Clicking the front

With Pick front points ticked, left-click points along the same front in two or more views. Points are drawn in each panel and are used by Refine fit:

  • a right-click removes that panel’s last point;

  • Undo point (Ctrl+Z) removes the point clicked last in any panel;

  • Clear points removes all of the edited model’s points on the displayed images;

  • untick Pick front points to navigate without adding points.

The GCS wireframe and Shock wireframe options hide a model temporarily so that the observed front can be inspected. Each model keeps its own front points.

Refining the fit

Refine fit (Ctrl+R) makes a local least-squares adjustment of the edited model through the clicked points. It refines a fit; it cannot find one from scratch, because longitude, α\alpha and κ\kappa are poorly conditioned in GCS, so first align the shell roughly with the CME by eye. The refinement fits as many parameters as the points support (Table 21.2); the status bar names the parameters fitted and how many more points would free the next one.

Staged refinement of the GCS model.
Front points Parameters fitted
2 Height
4, in two separated views Height, longitude, latitude
5 …and tilt
6 …and α\alpha
7 All six parameters (adding κ\kappa)

The status bar also reports the views taking part, their angular separations and the number of points. Only images within the Max time offset of the shared time take part. With a single view, or with no pair of views between 20° and 160° apart, the direction cannot be constrained and is held fixed; empty, nearly coincident and nearly opposite viewpoints do not constrain the direction independently. Formal errors are shown when the local solution is reliable, are withheld otherwise, and become invalid when the model or the observations change.

Recording fits

Commit GCS (Ctrl+Return) records the current fit at the shared time, together with the images it was made from and their observation details. Step to later times and repeat to build a height–time series. One combination of images cannot be recorded at two different times, so repeated images never count as independent height measurements.

When stepping, dragging the time slider or playing, the recorded shells are drawn: each fit on its own images, interpolated between recorded times (a display, not a fit) and held before the first and after the last record. A model with nothing recorded keeps its slider values, so commit before stepping away. Fit > Restore recorded model at current time and Delete recorded fit at current time revisit or remove a record; Fit > Reset model parameters resets the edited model.

Moving the event range to a different event sets the recorded fits aside. They return when you come back to that event, and the JSON export includes them.

Kinematics

The Kinematics card (Figure 21.2) lists the recorded fits of the edited model beside a height–time graph. For the GCS model the table shows Time (UT), t (s), Apex (R☉), Lon (°), Lat (°) and α (°); for the shock, κ\kappa replaces α\alpha.

  • Double-click a row to go back to its time and restore its model.

  • Choose a Linear, Quadratic or Cubic fit and click Fit height–time. A fit of degree nn needs n+1n+1 recorded times, and n+2n+2 before errors can be estimated (Section 18.4).

  • Clear fits removes the recorded fits of the edited model.

  • Export saves the table as CSV or the graph as a figure.

The heights are de-projected under the model assumptions, so the speeds are model-dependent radial speeds rather than plane-of-sky speeds.

Fitting the shock

Choose Edit: Shock to fit the shock with a Spheroid or an Ellipsoid (Figure 21.3). The parameters follow PyThea’s conventions exactly (Table 21.3).

Parameters of the shock model.
Slider Range Meaning
Lon, Lat as for GCS Stonyhurst direction of the shock center and apex.
Height 1.05–30 R⊙R_\odot Heliocentric distance of the apex (center distance plus the radial semi-axis aa).
κ\kappa 0.05–2.0 Self-similar constant κ=b/(h−1R⊙)\kappa = b/(h - 1\,R_\odot): the lateral size for a given apex height.
ε\varepsilon −0.99-0.99 to 0.990.99 Signed eccentricity: positive stretches the shock radially (a>ba > b), negative flattens it (a<ba < b).
Tilt −90∘-90^\circ to 90∘90^\circ Ellipsoid only: rotation about the radial axis; at 0 the bb axis is parallel to the solar equator.
α\alpha (b/c) 0.5–1.5 Ellipsoid only: ratio of the two lateral semi-axes.

The derived readout gives the center distance and the semi-axes, under PyThea’s names. Click the shock front and use Refine fit: the model’s exactly computed projected outline is pulled through the points in every view, with its own sequence of height, direction and shape parameters. Record shock fits with Commit Shock. The shock keeps its own front points, recorded fits, kinematics and CSV file. With fewer than three views, ε\varepsilon and the tilt are weakly constrained and an ellipsoid’s shape parameters trade off against each other, so prefer a spheroid.

Exporting results

Images and graphs are drawn again from the data rather than copied from the screen, always on a white page whatever the application theme; graphs follow the OriginPro style. Figures can be saved as PNG, PDF, EPS, SVG, TIFF or JPG.

Export analysis JSON…

(Ctrl+Shift+S) the current, recorded and set-aside parameters of both models, with the clicked points, image times, offsets and observer geometry. The file (schema version 2) has a shock section beside the GCS keys. It is an analysis export, not a PyThea session file.

Export recorded fits CSV…

the recorded series of the edited model (cme_gcs_fit.csv or cme_shock_fit.csv).

Export height–time graph…

the recorded apex heights with error bars and the chosen fit, titled with the model and fit, with the speed and acceleration in the legend.

Save viewpoint snapshot…

the three views as shown, with arcsecond axes, the wireframes, the solar limb, the front points and a note of where each drawn shell comes from. With the banners hidden, only each panel’s name is printed above it.

Export movie (GIF/MP4)…

every time step as playback shows it, recorded shells included, at the playback speed. MP4 needs the bundled FFmpeg; a GIF is offered when it is unavailable.

Export fitting report (PDF)…

the viewpoints and their separations, the model at the current time, every recorded fit drawn on the images it was made from with its parameters and observation details, each model’s linear, quadratic and cubic height–time fits (each with a titled graph and all its parameters, then compared), and the method, its limits and references (Figure 21.4).

Stepping through time for a movie or a report leaves the window as it was: the time shown, the working models, their formal errors and the front points are restored afterwards.

Scientific limits

GCS models the flux rope, not the shock. Formal fit errors leave out the uncertainty from identifying the front, non-simultaneous images, image preparation and the assumed geometry, and a small residual does not make a fit unique or accurate (Verbeke et al. 2023). Helioviewer JPEG2000 images are display products: suitable for fitting shapes, not for calibrated intensity measurements. Help > Fitting workflow and scientific limits… (F1) summarizes the procedure and these limits.

html:
File Formats and Outputs

Files read and written by the application

File types of the e-CALLISTO FITS Analyzer.
Extension Meaning
.fit, .fits, .fit.gz, .fits.gz Radio spectra in the main window, and solar images in Solar Image Analysis. Upper-case suffixes are accepted.
.efaproj Complete analyzer project: data, processing, view and analysis session (Section 10.1).
.efaview.json Portable view configuration: display range, units, thresholds, color map and graph styling (Section 7.2.2).
.ecsolar Solar Image Analysis session with embedded FITS frames (Section 16.4).
.srs Learmonth spectrograph daily archive file (Section 13.1).

Exported FITS files

A FITS file written with File > Export As > Export to FIT has the structure of a standard CALLISTO file:

Primary HDU

the two-dimensional spectrum (frequency ×\times time) with the chosen BITPIX, and the original header updated with the keywords in Table B.2.

AXIS extension

a binary table with one row and the columns FREQUENCY (MHz) and TIME (s).

Header keywords added or updated on FITS export.
Keyword Content
HISTORY “Exported by e-CALLISTO FITS Analyzer”, the plot type, the units shown, and the source file (or the first and last source of a combined dataset).
COMBINED T for a combined dataset, F otherwise.
COMBMETH Combination method: time, frequency or time_frequency.
NFILES Number of source files of a combined dataset.
BUNIT Intensity unit of the data.
DATAMIN, DATAMAX Minimum and maximum data values.
BSCALE, BZERO Scaling for integer data.

title: Data Sources
html:
Data Sources

Table C.1 lists the archives from which the application retrieves data. Access requires a network connection; most archives are public and need no registration, the exception being JSOC exports, which need a registered e-mail address. When you publish results based on these data, acknowledge the providers as their data policies request.

Archives used by the e-CALLISTO FITS Analyzer.

Note

Archive availability changes over time. The calibrated SOHO/LASCO and SOHO/EIT archives lag real time by many months, the HMI synoptic series is published about one Carrington rotation behind, and STEREO-B data end in 2014. Downloaded files are cached locally and can be reused without network access.

title: Models and Formulas
html:
Models and Formulas

This appendix collects the relations used to compute the quantities reported by the application. Heights rr are heliocentric distances in solar radii (R⊙=696340R_\odot = 696\,340 km), electron densities nen_e are in cm−3^{-3} and frequencies ff in MHz.

Intensity scales

CALLISTO digits to dB

the CALLISTO receiver’s logarithmic detector maps 2500 mV onto 256 digits with a slope of 25.4 mV/dB, so that ΔIdB=ΔIdigits×2500/(256×25.4)≈0.384\Delta I_\mathrm{dB} = \Delta I_\mathrm{digits}\times 2500/(256\times25.4)\approx 0.384 dB per digit. The Plotutil median-dB recipe used by Median (dB) and the batch processor uses 2500/(255×25.4)2500/(255\times25.4).

ARTEMIS-IV

40964096 ADC counts over a 70 dB range: 58.51 counts per dB.

GOES flare class

from the peak 0.1–0.8 nm flux FF: A for F<10−7F<10^{-7}, B for 10−7≤F<10−610^{-7}\le F<10^{-6}, C for 10−6≤F<10−510^{-6}\le F<10^{-5}, M for 10−5≤F<10−410^{-5}\le F<10^{-4} and X for F≥10−4F\ge10^{-4} W m−2^{-2}; the number is FF divided by the lower limit of the class (10−810^{-8} for A up to 10−410^{-4} for X), for example M2.5 for F=2.5×10−5F = 2.5\times10^{-5} W m−2^{-2}.

Radio burst analysis

Plasma frequency.

The fundamental emission frequency is the local plasma frequency fp=8.98×10−3neMHz,\begin{equation} f_p = 8.98\times10^{-3}\sqrt{n_e}\quad\text{MHz}, \end{equation} so ne=(f/8.98×10−3)2n_e = (f/8.98\times10^{-3})^2. For harmonic emission f=2fpf = 2f_p; the application divides the observed frequencies and drift rates by two before computing heights and speeds.

Coronal density models.

Each model is multiplied by the fold number NN (ne→Nnen_e \to N\,n_e).

Coronal electron-density models.
Model ne(r)n_e(r) in cm−3^{-3}
Newkirk 4.2×104×104.32/r4.2\times10^{4}\times10^{4.32/r}
Saito 1.36×106r−2.14+1.68×108r−6.131.36\times10^{6}\,r^{-2.14} + 1.68\times10^{8}\,r^{-6.13}
Leblanc 3.3×105r−2+4.1×106r−4+8.0×107r−63.3\times10^{5}\,r^{-2} + 4.1\times10^{6}\,r^{-4} + 8.0\times10^{7}\,r^{-6}
Baumbach–Allen 108(2.99r−16+1.55r−6+0.036r−1.5)10^{8}\left(2.99\,r^{-16} + 1.55\,r^{-6} + 0.036\,r^{-1.5}\right)
Mann 5.14×109exp⁡[13.83(1/r−1)]5.14\times10^{9}\exp\!\left[13.83\left(1/r - 1\right)\right]

For the Newkirk model the emission height has the closed form r=4.32ln⁡10ln⁡[ne/(N×4.2×104)].\begin{equation} r = \frac{4.32\,\ln 10}{\ln\!\left[n_e/(N\times4.2\times10^{4})\right]}. \end{equation} For the other models the height is found numerically between 1R⊙1\,R_\odot and 215 R⊙R_\odot (1 AU); frequencies outside this range have no height.

Power-law backbone and drift rate.

f(t)=a(t−t0)−b,dfdt=−ab(t−t0)−b−1.\begin{equation} f(t) = a\,(t-t_0)^{-b},\qquad \frac{\mathrm{d}f}{\mathrm{d}t} = -a\,b\,(t-t_0)^{-b-1}. \end{equation} The goodness of fit is reported as R2=1−∑(fi−f̂i)2/∑(fi−f‾)2R^2 = 1 - \sum(f_i-\hat f_i)^2/\sum(f_i-\bar f)^2 and RMSE=(fi−f̂i)2¯\mathrm{RMSE} = \sqrt{\overline{(f_i-\hat f_i)^2}}.

Shock speed.

v=R⊙|dfdt||drdf|,drdf=2nef|dne/dr|.\begin{equation} v = R_\odot\left|\frac{\mathrm{d}f}{\mathrm{d}t}\right|\left|\frac{\mathrm{d}r}{\mathrm{d}f}\right|, \qquad \frac{\mathrm{d}r}{\mathrm{d}f} = \frac{2\,n_e}{f\,\left|\mathrm{d}n_e/\mathrm{d}r\right|}. \end{equation} The initial values are evaluated at the starting frequency, the 90th percentile of the fitted frequencies; the average values are means along the backbone with their standard errors.

Band splitting

(Vršnak et al. 2002). X=(fufl)2,MA=X(X+5)2(4−X),VA=VsMA,B=VAμ0mpne(SI units; reported in gauss).\begin{gather} X = \left(\frac{f_u}{f_l}\right)^2,\qquad M_A = \sqrt{\frac{X\,(X+5)}{2\,(4-X)}},\qquad V_A = \frac{V_s}{M_A},\\ B = V_A\sqrt{\mu_0\,m_p\,n_e}\quad(\text{SI units; reported in gauss}). \end{gather}

Image measurements

Circle fit.

For a sphere of fitted radius rr resting on the solar surface, the height of its top is h=1R⊙+2rh = 1\,R_\odot + 2r.

Height–time fits.

linear:h=h0+vt,quadratic:h=h0+v0t+12at2,cubic:h=h0+v0t+12a0t2+16jt3.\begin{align} \text{linear:}\quad & h = h_0 + v\,t,\\ \text{quadratic:}\quad & h = h_0 + v_0\,t + \tfrac12 a\,t^2,\\ \text{cubic:}\quad & h = h_0 + v_0\,t + \tfrac12 a_0\,t^2 + \tfrac16 j\,t^3. \end{align} Uncertainties are propagated from the covariance of the fitted coefficients.

Three-dimensional CME models

GCS

(Thernisien et al. 2006; Thernisien 2011). Parameters: Stonyhurst longitude and latitude of the propagation direction, tilt, leading-edge height hh, half-angle α\alpha and aspect ratio κ\kappa. Intrinsic widths: wface-on=2[α+arcsinκ],wedge-on=2arcsin⁡κ.\begin{equation} w_\text{face-on} = 2\left[\alpha + \arcsin\kappa\right],\qquad w_\text{edge-on} = 2\arcsin\kappa. \end{equation}

Shock spheroid and ellipsoid

(Kouloumvakos et al. 2022). With the radial semi-axis aa and lateral semi-axes bb and cc: h=rcenter+a,κ=bh−1R⊙,ε={+1−(b/a)2a>b,−1−(a/b)2a<b,α=bc.\begin{equation} h = r_\text{center} + a,\qquad \kappa = \frac{b}{h - 1\,R_\odot},\qquad \varepsilon = \begin{cases} +\sqrt{1-(b/a)^2} & a > b,\\ -\sqrt{1-(a/b)^2} & a < b,\end{cases} \qquad \alpha = \frac{b}{c}. \end{equation} A spheroid has c=bc = b (α=1\alpha = 1, no tilt).

title: Troubleshooting

headings.title:
Solar Image Analysis and
GCS fitting

html:
Troubleshooting

Main window

Buttons and menu items are grayed out.

Most analysis controls, and the Graph Properties panel, are enabled only after a file is loaded. Isolate Burst additionally requires background subtraction.

Rectangle zoom does nothing.

Click Lock zooming and panning first, then Rectangular Zooming, and drag a rectangle. Each activation allows one rectangle.

Drift-rate picking does not stop.

Right-click or double-click to finish the series of points.

Selected files cannot be combined.

The message names the reason — for example non-consecutive timestamps, mixed stations or an incomplete time ×\times focus-code grid. Check the rules in Table 5.1.

The UT time axis is unavailable.

UT display, UT display ranges and UT alignment in the Multi-Station Comparison need the TIME-OBS keyword in the FITS header. Use seconds instead.

The thresholds were reset after background subtraction.

Limits chosen on raw data would saturate the background-subtracted scale and are therefore reset. Set them again, or apply a preset.

The application closed unexpectedly.

Restart it and accept the offer to recover the autosave snapshot, or use File > Recover Last Session....

A save fails on Windows.

The proposed folder may not be writable (for example inside C:
Program Files); choose another folder when asked.

Downloads and archives

The station list is empty or a station is missing.

Station lists contain only stations with data on the selected UTC days. Check the date and the network connection.

A listed burst has no FITS files.

Catalog detections do not guarantee that matching files are archived. Increase Extra time, or search another station.

Recent SOHO/LASCO or SOHO/EIT data cannot be found.

The calibrated archives lag real time by many months. Use Find Latest to locate the newest archived data, or Live Preview (Helioviewer) for recent quicklook images.

JSOC downloads, binned frames or cutouts are refused.

Enter a JSOC notify e-mail registered at https://jsoc.stanford.edu/ajax/register_email.html in the Data Source card. Binned and cutout frame sizes require the JSOC source.

The disk is filling up.

Empty the caches with the Clear Cache buttons of the e-CALLISTO Downloader and the SunPy Explorer, or with Data > Reset All (clear cache & defaults) in Solar Image Analysis.

Solar Image Analysis and GCS fitting

The PFSS card is disabled.

When running from source, install the sunkit-magex package; the card shows the command.

Clicked PFSS seeds or the crop rectangle do not respond.

These interactions need the PyQtGraph renderer (Display & Crop card).

A GCS panel reports that it has no data.

The STEREO-B archive ends on 27 September 2014. Switch that panel to another channel.

GCS refinement does not change the direction.

The direction is constrained only by at least four points in two views separated by 20°–160°. Add points in a second, well-separated view.

MP4 export is not offered.

MP4 export needs FFmpeg, which is bundled with the installers. If it is unavailable, save a GIF instead.

Installation

macOS reports that the application cannot be verified.

Open System Settings > Privacy & Security and click Open Anyway, or Control-click the application and choose Open.

The application does not start on Linux.

Install the package with apt, which also installs the required Qt/OpenGL libraries (libgl1, libegl1, libxkbcommon-x11-0, libxcb-cursor0).

Qt reports “DLL load failed” when running from source on Windows.

Rebuild the virtual environment with packaging/windows/repair_windows_venv.ps1.

If a problem persists, report it with About > Report a Bug... (Section 4.4).

title: Glossary
html:
Glossary

Air Force Data Assimilative Photospheric Flux Transport model; synoptic magnetograms that estimate the unobserved far side of the Sun.

Atmospheric Imaging Assembly on SDO; full-disk EUV and UV imager.

Ratio of the shock speed to the Alfvén speed.

Speed of Alfvén waves, B/μ0ρB/\sqrt{\mu_0\rho}; depends on the magnetic field and plasma density.

Solar radio spectrograph at Thermopylae, Greece.

Removal of each frequency channel’s steady receiver and sky level from a dynamic spectrum.

Division of a Type II emission lane into two parallel bands emitted upstream and downstream of the shock.

Each image minus the first image of the sequence.

FITS keyword giving the data type of the stored values.

Heliographic coordinates that rotate with the Sun at the Carrington rate; used for synoptic maps.

Coordinated Data Analysis Workshop data center at NASA GSFC, host of the SOHO/LASCO CME catalog.

Coronal mass ejection: an eruption of magnetized plasma from the corona.

Ratio of the downstream to the upstream plasma density at a shock.

Telescope that blocks the solar disk with an occulter to observe the faint corona.

Function ne(r)n_e(r) giving the coronal electron density at a heliocentric distance.

Compensation for solar differential rotation over an image sequence.

Raw CALLISTO intensity value (analog-to-digital converter unit, ADU), about 0.384 dB per digit.

Rate of change of the emission frequency of a burst, df/dt\mathrm{d}f/\mathrm{d}t.

Disturbance storm-time index; measure of the ring current and geomagnetic storm strength.

Radio intensity as a function of frequency and time.

World-wide network of CALLISTO solar radio spectrometers.

Extreme-ultraviolet Imaging Telescope on SOHO.

Extreme ultraviolet.

Extreme Ultraviolet Imager of STEREO/SECCHI.

Flexible Image Transport System, the standard astronomical data format.

Two-digit identifier of a CALLISTO receiver or frequency band at a station.

Factor multiplying a coronal density model to represent denser structures.

Plasma emission at the local plasma frequency, or at twice it.

Graduated Cylindrical Shell, a geometric flux-rope model of CMEs.

Global Oscillation Network Group, a ground-based network providing synoptic magnetograms.

Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites of NOAA, carrying the XRS, SGPS and SUVI instruments.

Heliophysics Event Knowledgebase.

Observer-centered angular coordinates on the sky, in arcseconds from Sun center.

Service providing JPEG2000 solar images for browsing.

Heliospheric Imagers (HI1, HI2) of STEREO/SECCHI.

Helioseismic and Magnetic Imager on SDO.

Time–elongation map built from a slit through a sequence of images.

Joint Science Operations Center, the SDO data archive.

Planetary three-hourly index of geomagnetic activity, from 0 to 9.

Large Angle and Spectrometric Coronagraph (C2, C3) on SOHO.

Processing levels of solar image data, from archive products to registered or composite images.

Normalizing-radial-graded filter, which flattens the radial brightness gradient of coronagraph images.

Disk in a coronagraph that blocks the bright inner field of view.

Magnetic field lines that reach the source surface, or return to the photosphere.

The publication graph style used for exported figures: closed frame, inward ticks and a white background.

Potential-field source-surface model of the coronal magnetic field.

Natural oscillation frequency of electrons in a plasma, fp≈8.98nef_p \approx 8.98\sqrt{n_e} kHz.

Angle on the sky measured from solar north toward east.

Function of the form at−ba\,t^{-b}.

Solar radius, 696 340 km.

Radio-frequency interference from terrestrial transmitters.

The line of peak intensity of a burst in a dynamic spectrum.

Each image minus the previous image.

Solar Dynamics Observatory.

Sun Earth Connection Coronal and Heliospheric Investigation on STEREO (EUVI, COR1, COR2, HI1, HI2).

Solar energetic particles.

Solar and Galactic Proton Sensor on GOES-R series satellites.

Solar and Heliospheric Observatory.

Sphere in the PFSS model beyond which the field is radial.

Solar Terrestrial Relations Observatory (Ahead and Behind spacecraft).

Heliographic coordinates with longitude zero facing the Earth.

Solar Ultraviolet Imager on GOES.

Radio and plasma wave instrument on STEREO.

Full-Sun map assembled over a solar rotation.

Slowly drifting radio burst produced by a shock wave.

Fast-drifting radio burst produced by electron beams.

Universal Time.

Virtual Solar Observatory.

X-Ray Sensor on GOES, with short (0.05–0.4 nm) and long (0.1–0.8 nm) channels.
